full_judgment:
Mr. M. M. Ruhul Amin, J.: This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 04.04.2004 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.899 of 1998 discharging the Rule. 

2. Short facts are that the plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 272 of 1987 in the court of Senior Assistant Judge, Barisal for a decree for partition with a prayer for declaration that the kabala dated 23.12.1920 in favour of the defendant is void stating, inter alia, that 60 decimals of land of Mouza Kashipur under R.S. Khatian No.2044 P.S. Barisal Sadar belonged to Nasaruddin in 16 annas and 12 decimals of land of C.S. Khatian No. 199 of the same mouza belonged to Sona Gazi and Nasaruddin in 8 annas share each. 48 decimals of land of C.S. Khatian No.146, 3.03 decimals of land of C.S. Khatian No.161, 13 decimals of land of C.S. Khatian No.226, 91 decimals of land of C.S. Khatian No.240, 1.23 decimals of land of C.S. Khatian No.241, 6 decimals of land of C.S. Khatian No.293 belonged to Nasaruddin alone and C.S. record was correctly prepared and finally published. Nasaruddin died leaving behind his only son Hamijuddin who inherited the property. After his death, Sarbanu and her daughter Somartaban inherited 2 annas 13 gondas 1 kara 1 kranti and out of the remaining land, the brother of Sarbanu inherited 2 annas 13 gandas 1 kara 1 kranti. Somartaban died leaving behind two sons and two daughters as her heirs who inherited her share. The share of Hamijuddin was inherited by his sons and daughters, defendant Nos.1-6. Sarbanu had no other name like Sawrupjan and Sarbanu was never married to Ludu Mollah. Hamijuddin in order to deprive his full sister, Somartaban Bibi created a forged, fabricated document on 23.12.1920 and no possession was delivered and no consideration money passed. When Somarthaban Bibi was given in marriage with Safar Molla her husband Safar Molla erected homestead in a portion of the land wherein Hamijuddin lived with his wife Somarthaban Bibi. After the death of Safar Mollah, plaintiff had been residing in the suit land. Record of right was not prepared in the name of Sarbanu but it was prepared in the name of Hamijuddin who had no possession in the entire suit land. Hamijuddin collusively got the record of rights prepared in his name and there is no basis for R.S. and S.A. record. Hence the suit. 

3. Defendant Nos.2.3 and 6 filed a joint written statement and defendant Nos.27-29 filed another written statement. The case of the defendant Nos.2, 3 and 6 is that Nasaruddin died leaving behind his son Hamijuddin and one daughter Sarbanu @ Sawrupjan Bibi and wife Arabjan who inherited his share. Hamijuddin inherited his share and his, daughter Sawraupjan inherited 4 annas share and his first wife Arabjan Bibi got 2 annas share. Sawrupjan Bibi was given in marriage with Babar Mollah and they had two sons and one daughter in the wedlock. After the death of Babar Mollah, Sawrupjan Bibi was again married to Ludu Mollah and after the death of Sawrupjan her property was inherited by her daughter Samarthaban Bibi and her husband Ludu Mollah and mother Arabjan Bibi. Two sons of Swarupjan Bibi died unmarried. Arabjan Bibi transferred her share to the predecessor of these defendants on 13th Boishakh, 1319 B.S. by Heba deed and afterwards she sold her land inherited from her daughter to Hamijuddin by another deed. Thereafter Somarthaban Bibi and Ludu Mollah sold 9 gonda 2 kranti share on 23.12.1920 to the predecessor of the defendant and delivered possession. At the time of preparation of S.A. record the same was correctly prepared in their names. 

4. The case of the defendant Nos.27-29 is that after the death of Hamijuddin, his son, defendant No. 1 transferred 14 decimals of land on 26.11.1980 and his daughter Pakinnessa transferred 7 decimals of land on 29.03.1987 to the defendants and since then they have been possessing the same by constructing a building. They also purchased 21/2  decimals of 2 land from Plot No.1242 from Pakimunnessa by kabalas dated 19.10.1980 and 29.03.1987. They also purchased 41/2  decimals of land 2 from Plot No.1242 from Belaluddin Howlader. Belaluddin sold 43/4 decimals of land to 4 Morshed Hossain on 26.11.1980. Haji Adam Ali purchased 7 decimals of land from Asia Khatun wife of Hasan Ali Mollah from Plot No.1242 on 06.11.1969. Adam Ali sold 07 decimals of land to the contesting defendant and they are in possession. 

5. The learned Assistant Judge on consideration of the materials on record decreed the suit in part holding that Ext.6=Ext. Kha was executed only by Ludu Molla and not by Samarthaban Bibi and as such her property was not transferred by this document. The defendants then preferred Title Appeal No.2 of 1996 and the court of appeal allowed the appeal and dismissed the suit holding that Somorthaban Bibi duly executed Ext.6=Ext. Kha and as such her share was duly transferred by this document. The plaintiff then preferred the above mentioned civil revisional application and the Rule was discharged. 

6. We have heard Dr. M. Zahir, the learned Counsel for the petitioner and perused the judgment of the High Court Division and other connected papers. 

7. Dr. Zahir argued that Ext.6=Ext. Kha was executed by Ludu Mollah by putting his signature and Somorthaban Bibi putting L.T.I but in the first page of certified copy Ext.6 there is nothing to show that Somorthaban Bibi put L.T.I. although from the second page of certified copy of the documents it appears that Somorthaban Bibi duly appeared before the sub-registrar concerned and admitted execution of the document and she was duly identified before the sub-registrar. The court of appeal below and the High Court Division concurrently held that since from the body of the document it is clear that two persons executed the document Ext.6=Ext. Kha and the name of Somorthaban Bibi appeared as one of the executants in the body of the document. From the other pages of the document it is clear that she put L.T.I. as executant in the document and the concerned Sub-registrar gave endorsement in the document itself that Somorthaban Bibi appeared before him and admitted execution of the document and she was duly identified before Sub-registrar. Accordingly, the court of appeal which is the final court of fact and the High Court Division held that the Ext.6=Ext. Kha was duly executed by Somorthaban Bibi and it is a valid document. 

8. Dr. M. Zahir then submits that D.W.4 Helaluddin in his evidence stated that the plaintiff has been in possession of .07 decimals of land in the homestead but the suit of the plaintiff as a whole was dismissed and as such the court of appeal and the High Court Division committed error of law occasioning failure of justice. It appears that this 07 decimals of land is from other Khatian which has not been included in the schedule of the plaint. 

9. Dr. M. Zahir lastly submits that since the possession of the plaintiffs in .07 decimals of land is admitted by D.W.4, they are entitled to get a decree on the basis of adverse possession. But as it appears no case of adverse possession was made out in the pleading and was proved and the plea of adverse possession has been raised for the first time before this court. It is the settled principle of law that the plea of adverse possession must be specifically pleaded in the pleading and proved by evidence. 

10. In view of the discussion above, we are of the view that the High Court Division did not commit any error of law requiring interference by this court. 

11. Accordingly, this petition is dismissed. 

End.
